question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

France is a largest country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. large.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contains the indefinite article "a". An indefinite article can never be used with a superlative degree, because a superlative singles out one particular thing and therefore demands the definite article "the" (the largest, the smallest, the best).

◦ Incorrect: France is a largest country.

◦ Correct: France is a large country.

• Here there is no comparison at all in the sentence — no "than" and no group is mentioned. So the positive degree "large" is the only grammatically fit option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "smaller" and Option 2 "larger" are comparative forms; a comparative needs "than" (France is larger than Nepal), which is absent here.

• Option 3 "smallest" is a superlative and repeats the very error of the original sentence — it would still need "the", and it also reverses the sense.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: large – larger – largest.

◦ Positive: used when no comparison is made — "France is a large country."

◦ Comparative: used to compare two things, always with "than" — "France is larger than Italy."

◦ Superlative: used to compare more than two, always with "the" — "Russia is the largest country in the world."

• Rule to remember: a/an + superlative = wrong; the + superlative = right.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Mr Sharma would have left / the station / by this time / tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mr Sharma would have left.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The time marker "by this time tomorrow" points to a moment in the future. An action that will be completed before a given future time must be expressed in the future perfect tense — "will have + V3".

◦ Incorrect: Mr Sharma would have left the station by this time tomorrow.

◦ Correct: Mr Sharma will have left the station by this time tomorrow.

• "Would have + V3" is a past unreal/conditional form (used for something that did not actually happen — "He would have left if he had got a ticket"). It clashes with the future adverbial "tomorrow".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "the station" is a correct noun phrase with the definite article.

• "by this time" is the correct prepositional phrase for a deadline ("by" = not later than).

• "tomorrow" is the correct future adverb of time and needs no preposition.

NOTE

• Future perfect = will/shall have + past participle. Signal words: by tomorrow, by next month, by 2030, by the time, by then.

◦ By next June, she will have completed her degree.

• Do not confuse: will have + V3 (future perfect) vs would have + V3 (unfulfilled past condition, third conditional).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

“Do not turn a blind eye to all the mischief your child is up to”, the teacher told the young parent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pretend not to notice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to turn a blind eye (to something)" means to deliberately ignore something wrong; to pretend not to see or notice it. (जानबूझकर अनदेखा करना)

◦ In the sentence the teacher warns the parent not to ignore the child's mischief — i.e., not to pretend not to notice it.

◦ Example: The guard turned a blind eye to the students sneaking out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Close the door" is a literal action and has nothing to do with ignoring wrongdoing.

• Option 2 "Take pride in" means to feel satisfaction about something — the opposite of ignoring.

• Option 3 "Give rewards" means to reward, which does not match "Do not ..." in a warning about mischief.

NOTE

• Origin: the phrase is popularly traced to Admiral Horatio Nelson, who is said to have put his telescope to his blind eye at the Battle of Copenhagen (1801) so that he could claim not to have seen the signal to retreat.

• Related idioms of ignoring: "look the other way", "turn a deaf ear" (refuse to listen), "sweep under the carpet" (hide a problem), "give the cold shoulder" (ignore a person deliberately).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The mother ________ the chips because they were soggy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. discarded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Discard" means to throw away / get rid of something that is no longer wanted or is unfit for use. (फेंक देना)

• The reason clause "because they were soggy" (limp, damp and unappetising) explains why the chips had to be thrown away.

◦ Correct: The mother discarded the chips because they were soggy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "saved" (kept for later) contradicts the reason given — nobody keeps soggy chips.

• Option 2 "wasted" means to use carelessly/squander; it usually needs an object like money, time or an opportunity, and it blames the mother rather than describing disposal. It does not fit the logic of "because they were soggy".

• Option 4 "recovered" (got back something lost) is illogical here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of discard: throw away, dispose of, jettison, dump, scrap, cast off. Antonyms: keep, retain, preserve, save.

• Word usage: "soggy" = unpleasantly wet and soft (सीला हुआ); its opposite for snacks is "crisp/crunchy".

question:
Identify the most appropriate meaning of the given word.

Hope
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Wish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hope" means a feeling of expectation and desire for a particular thing to happen; to want something to be true. Its closest meaning among the options is "wish" — a desire for something. (आशा / इच्छा)

◦ Example: I hope/wish to see you soon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Caution" means care taken to avoid danger (सावधानी) — unrelated.

• Option 2 "Realism" means seeing and accepting things as they really are (यथार्थवाद) — it is about facts, not desire.

• Option 3 "Cynicism" means a distrustful, negative attitude that believes people act only from selfish motives (निंदावाद) — it is the opposite in spirit to hope.

NOTE

• Synonyms of hope: wish, desire, aspiration, expectation, optimism, longing, anticipation.

• Antonyms of hope: despair, hopelessness, pessimism, cynicism, dejection.

• Grammar note: "hope" is followed by a that-clause or a to-infinitive ("I hope that he wins", "I hope to win"), whereas "wish" for an unreal situation takes the past subjunctive ("I wish I were rich").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Have egg on your face
option_2: To be made to look foolish or embarrassed
option_3: Making a choice between two unpleasant choices
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To be made to look foolish or embarrassed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to have egg on one's face" means to be made to look foolish, embarrassed or humiliated, usually because of something one said or did that went wrong. (शर्मिंदा होना / मूर्ख दिखना)

◦ Example: The minister had egg on his face when his own figures were proved wrong in Parliament.

• The image behind it is of a person who has literally been hit with an egg — publicly ridiculed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Defeat someone thoroughly" is the meaning of idioms like "beat hollow" / "wipe the floor with someone".

• Option 3 "Making a choice between two unpleasant choices" is the meaning of "between the devil and the deep blue sea" or "Hobson's choice / a catch-22".

• Option 4 "Reveal a secret" is the meaning of "let the cat out of the bag" or "spill the beans".

NOTE

• Related idioms of embarrassment: "red-faced", "eat humble pie" (to admit one was wrong and apologise), "eat one's words", "lose face" (to lose respect).

question:
The following sentence contains some errors. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The tiger was tranquiliized in the morning and keept in a cage to avoid disturbannces by human beings.
option_1: The tiger was tranquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoiid disturbaences by human beings.
option_2: The tiger was tranquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoid disturbances by human beings.
option_3: The tiger was traanquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoid dissturbances by human beings.
option_4: The tiger was tranquiliized in the morning and keept in a cage to avoid disturbances by human beings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The tiger was tranquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoid disturbances by human beings.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence contains three spelling errors: "tranquiliized", "keept" and "disturbannces". The option that corrects all three at once, without introducing any new mistake, is the right answer.

◦ "tranquiliized" → "tranquilized" (made calm/sedated with a drug)

◦ "keept" → "kept" (past tense of "keep": keep – kept – kept)

◦ "disturbannces" → "disturbances" (interruptions/disorder)

• Only Option 2 is completely error-free: "The tiger was tranquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoid disturbances by human beings."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 corrects "tranquilized" and "kept" but adds two new errors — "avoiid" and "disturbaences".

• Option 3 wrongly spells "traanquilized" and "dissturbances".

• Option 4 leaves the original errors "tranquiliized" and "keept" untouched.

NOTE

• Strategy for such questions: mark each misspelt word in the question sentence, then reject every option that still carries an error or that adds a fresh one; exactly one option will be clean.

• Spelling note: "tranquilize/tranquilise" (American "tranquilizer", British "tranquilliser") comes from "tranquil" = calm and peaceful.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

She’s reading a ________(secrecy) novel and can’t wait to find out who the killer is.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. mystery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed clue word is "secrecy" — the state of keeping something hidden or unknown. The word that carries this sense and also names a type of novel is "mystery". (रहस्य)

• The second half of the sentence, "can't wait to find out who the killer is", is the classic description of a mystery novel (a whodunit).

◦ Correct: She's reading a mystery novel and can't wait to find out who the killer is.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "crisis" means a time of intense difficulty or danger (संकट) — there is no such collocation as a "crisis novel".

• Option 2 "complication" means something that makes a situation more difficult (जटिलता) — it does not mean secrecy.

• Option 3 "difficulty" means hardship or trouble (कठिनाई) — again unrelated to something hidden.

NOTE

• Synonyms of mystery: enigma, riddle, puzzle, secret, conundrum.

• Genres of fiction often asked in SSC exams: mystery/thriller (suspense, crime), fiction, non-fiction, science fiction, fantasy, biography/autobiography, satire.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

The viable of life / depends on a pair / of conflicting realities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The viable of life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Viable" is an adjective (meaning capable of working successfully / able to survive). After the definite article "The" and before "of life", the sentence needs a noun, not an adjective.

• The correct noun form is "viability" (the ability to survive or succeed).

◦ Incorrect: The viable of life depends on a pair of conflicting realities.

◦ Correct: The viability of life depends on a pair of conflicting realities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "depends on a pair" is correct — the verb "depend" always takes the preposition "on/upon".

• "of conflicting realities" is a correct prepositional phrase ("conflicting" is a participial adjective before the plural noun "realities").

• Since a clear error exists, "No error" (Option 2) cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Word-form family: viable (adjective) – viability (noun) – viably (adverb).

• Similar adjective → noun conversions often tested: able → ability, stable → stability, probable → probability, responsible → responsibility, flexible → flexibility.

• Rule: after "the ... of", a noun is required (the strength of, the beauty of, the viability of).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

I shall be playing for four hours.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. shall be playing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "for four hours" states the duration of an action. When a period of time introduced by "for" is mentioned, the continuous tense must be replaced by the perfect continuous tense.

• So the future continuous "shall be playing" must become the future perfect continuous "shall have been playing".

◦ Incorrect: I shall be playing for four hours.

◦ Correct: I shall have been playing for four hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "I" is the correct first-person subject pronoun and correctly takes "shall".

• "for" is the correct preposition before a period of time.

• "four hours" is a correct plural time expression.

NOTE

• Rule: since/for + time with a continuing action requires the perfect continuous tense.

◦ Present perfect continuous: He has been playing for four hours.

◦ Past perfect continuous: He had been playing for four hours.

◦ Future perfect continuous: He will/shall have been playing for four hours.

• "Since" is used with a point of time (since 5 o'clock, since Monday) and "for" with a period of time (for four hours, for two years).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Our team is all on the same page when it comes to our goals for the upcoming project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Be in agreement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to be on the same page" means to be in agreement; to share the same understanding, opinion or plan about something. (एकमत होना)

◦ In the sentence, the whole team agrees about the goals of the coming project.

◦ Example: Before we start work, let us make sure everyone is on the same page.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Be confused" and Option 3 "Be unsure" describe a lack of clarity, not agreement.

• Option 4 "Be in conflict" is the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• The image behind the idiom is of several people reading from the very same page of a book, so they see exactly the same thing.

• Similar idioms of agreement: "see eye to eye", "in tune with", "of one mind", "hit it off".

• Opposite idioms: "at loggerheads", "at odds with", "at cross purposes".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Bite the dust
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To suffer a defeat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to bite the dust" means to be defeated, to fail, to come to an end, or (in some contexts) to die. (हार जाना / परास्त होना)

◦ Example: Another small shop bit the dust when the mall opened nearby.

◦ Example: The champion finally bit the dust in the semi-final.

• The literal picture is of a fallen warrior lying face down and taking dust into the mouth.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "To fall from a height" is only the literal image, not the idiomatic meaning.

• Option 3 "To remain calm" corresponds to idioms like "keep one's cool" or "hold your horses".

• Option 4 "To fall asleep" corresponds to "hit the sack / hit the hay".

NOTE

• Similar idioms of defeat/failure: "go down in flames", "come a cropper", "meet one's Waterloo", "throw in the towel" (to give up).

• Idioms of success (opposite): "come out on top", "carry the day", "with flying colours".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who avoids sensory pleasures and physical comforts
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Ascetic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "ascetic" is a person who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from all forms of indulgence, sensory pleasure and physical comfort, usually for religious or spiritual reasons. (तपस्वी / संन्यासी)

◦ Example: The ascetic lived on fruit and water in a mountain cave.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Frugal" is an adjective meaning sparing/economical with money and food (मितव्ययी). It refers to thrift, not to renouncing pleasure on principle.

• Option 2 "Epicurean" is the exact opposite — a person devoted to sensual enjoyment, especially good food and drink (भोगवादी).

• Option 3 "Bohemian" is a person who lives an unconventional, artistic and socially free lifestyle — not one who denies himself comforts.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes frequently asked in SSC exams:

◦ Hermit / Recluse – one who lives alone, away from society

◦ Stoic – one who endures pain or hardship without complaint

◦ Hedonist – one who believes pleasure is the chief good in life

◦ Misanthrope – one who hates mankind

◦ Philanthropist – one who loves and helps mankind

• Word family: ascetic (noun/adjective) – asceticism (noun) – ascetically (adverb).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Conffess.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conffess" is misspelt — it has a wrongly doubled "f". The correct spelling is "confess", meaning to admit or acknowledge one's fault, crime or secret. (स्वीकार करना / कबूल करना)

◦ Spelling key: CON + FESS (one "f", double "s").

◦ Example: The accused finally confessed to the theft.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Chivalrous" (Option 1) is correctly spelt — it means courteous, gallant and honourable, especially towards women (शिष्ट / वीर).

• "Expose" (Option 2) is correctly spelt — to uncover, reveal or make something visible (उजागर करना).

• "Convict" (Option 4) is correctly spelt — as a verb, to declare someone guilty; as a noun, a person found guilty of a crime (दोषी ठहराना / अपराधी).

NOTE

• Word family of confess: confess (verb) – confession (noun) – confessor (noun) – confessedly (adverb).

• Watch out for common double-letter traps: necessary (one "c", two "s"), accommodate (two "c", two "m"), occurrence (two "c", two "r"), embarrass (two "r", two "s").

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person living in solitude like a saint for religious practices.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Hermit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "hermit" is a person who lives alone in solitude, away from society, usually for religious reasons. (संन्यासी / एकांतवासी)

◦ Example: The old hermit had not spoken to anyone for twenty years.

• The definition given — "living in solitude like a saint for religious practices" — is the textbook meaning of a hermit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Cretin" is a very stupid or foolish person (an offensive term) — unrelated to solitude.

• Option 3 "Heir" is a person legally entitled to inherit the property or rank of another (उत्तराधिकारी).

• Option 4 "Heretic" is a person whose belief goes against the accepted doctrine of a religion (विधर्मी) — a hermit follows religion, a heretic opposes its orthodoxy.

NOTE

• Closely related one-word substitutes:

◦ Recluse – a person who lives alone and avoids other people

◦ Ascetic – one who abstains from worldly pleasures for spiritual reasons

◦ Monk / Nun – a member of a religious community

◦ Pilgrim – one who travels to a holy place

◦ Martyr – one who dies for a cause or faith

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Clumsy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Graceful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Clumsy" means awkward in movement or handling things; lacking skill or grace. (भद्दा / अनाड़ी)

• Its antonym is "graceful", meaning moving in a smooth, elegant and attractive way. (सुंदर / लालित्यपूर्ण)

◦ Example: The clumsy waiter dropped the tray, while the graceful dancer glided across the stage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Jealous" means resentful of someone else's success or possessions (ईर्ष्यालु) — unrelated to physical co-ordination.

• Option 2 "Fierce" means violent, aggressive or intense (उग्र) — unrelated.

• Option 4 "Nervous" means anxious or easily agitated (घबराया हुआ). Nervousness may cause clumsiness, but it is not its opposite.

NOTE

• Synonyms of clumsy: awkward, ungainly, gawky, bungling, maladroit, inept, lumbering.

• Antonyms of clumsy: graceful, dexterous, deft, adroit, nimble, agile, skilful.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

No sooner had the sun risen over the horizon when the birds began to chirp and the squirrels started to scamper around the park.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. than the birds began.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "No sooner" is always followed by "than", never by "when" or "then". The fixed pair is "No sooner ... than ...".

• Also, "No sooner" at the beginning of a sentence causes inversion — the auxiliary comes before the subject ("No sooner had the sun risen"), which the sentence has already done correctly.

• Tense sequence: the first clause is in the past perfect ("had risen"), so the clause after "than" must be in the simple past — "began", not "begin".

• The definite article "the" is needed before "birds" because specific birds of that place are meant, matching "the squirrels" later in the sentence.

◦ Correct: No sooner had the sun risen over the horizon than the birds began to chirp and the squirrels started to scamper around the park.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "when the birds begin" keeps the wrong conjunction "when" and also uses the present tense "begin".

• Option 2 "than birds begin" has the right conjunction but a wrong tense ("begin") and drops "the".

• Option 3 "when birds began" keeps the wrong conjunction "when" and drops "the".

NOTE

• Important conjunction pairs for SSC exams:

◦ No sooner ... than – No sooner did he sit down than the phone rang.

◦ Hardly / Scarcely ... when (or before) – Hardly had he sat down when the phone rang.

◦ Barely ... when – Barely had we started when it rained.

◦ Such ... that, So ... that, Rather ... than, Not only ... but also, Lest ... should

• Remember: "No sooner" takes "than", but "Hardly/Scarcely" take "when/before".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

During the meeting, he went on a long and angry _______ about how the project was being mismanaged.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. rant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "rant" is a long, loud, angry speech of complaint or criticism. (लंबा गुस्से भरा भाषण)

• The adjectives "long and angry" and the collocation "went on a ... rant" fix the answer — one "goes on a rant" about something one is furious about.

◦ Correct: During the meeting, he went on a long and angry rant about how the project was being mismanaged.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "shout" is a single loud cry, not a long continuous speech; "a long shout" does not collocate with "went on a".

• Option 2 "whisper" is speech in a very soft voice — it contradicts "angry" and "long".

• Option 4 "mutter" is low, indistinct, half-audible speech — again the opposite of a loud outburst.

NOTE

• Collocations: "go on a rant", "rant and rave" (to speak angrily and at length).

• Synonyms of rant: tirade, diatribe, harangue, fulmination, outburst.

• Word family: rant (noun/verb) – ranting (adjective/noun) – ranter (noun).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I had / a bad habit of / waking up / lately.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. lately.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lately" means "recently / in the recent past" (हाल ही में) — it is an adverb of time, not of manner.

• The sense required here is "waking up late" (i.e., not early). "Late" itself works both as an adjective and as an adverb of time, so no "-ly" is needed.

◦ Incorrect: I had a bad habit of waking up lately.

◦ Correct: I had a bad habit of waking up late.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "I had" is a correct subject + verb combination in the past tense.

• "a bad habit of" is a correct noun phrase — "habit" is always followed by the preposition "of".

• "waking up" is correct because a preposition ("of") must be followed by a gerund (V-ing).

NOTE

• Adverbs that change meaning when "-ly" is added (a favourite SSC topic):

◦ late (not on time) vs lately (recently)

◦ hard (with effort) vs hardly (almost not)

◦ near (close) vs nearly (almost)

◦ short (abruptly) vs shortly (soon)

◦ high (at a great height) vs highly (very much)

◦ most (superlative) vs mostly (mainly)

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Chaitnya was __________ from the school due to his misappropriate behaviour.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. expelled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Expelled" means officially forced to leave a school, organisation or country as a punishment. (निष्कासित करना / निकाल देना)

• It is the only correctly spelt option: EX + PEL + LED — the final "l" of "expel" is doubled before "-ed" because the verb ends in a single consonant preceded by a stressed vowel.

◦ Correct: Chaitnya was expelled from the school due to his misappropriate behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "xpelled" and 4 "xpeled" wrongly drop the initial "e".

• Option 3 "expeled" wrongly uses a single "l" before "-ed".

NOTE

• Doubling rule: for verbs ending in a single vowel + single consonant with the stress on the last syllable, double the final consonant before "-ed/-ing" — expel → expelled/expelling, compel → compelled, refer → referred, prefer → preferred, begin → beginning, permit → permitted.

• Word family: expel (verb) – expulsion (noun) – expelled (past/participle). Related words: rusticate (to suspend a student temporarily), suspend, debar, oust, banish.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Once there was a king named Midas who was granted a (1)________ by Dionysus, the god of wine. For his wish, Midas asked that whatever he (2)________ would turn to gold. Despite Dionysus’ efforts to prevent it, Midas pleaded that this was a fantastic wish, and so, it was bestowed. Excited about his newly-earned (3)________, Midas started touching all kinds of things, turning each item into pure gold. But soon, Midas became (4)________. As he picked up a piece of food, he found he couldn’t eat it. It had turned to gold in his hand. Hungry, Midas groaned, “I’ll starve! Perhaps this was not such an excellent wish after all!” Seeing his dismay, Midas’ (5)________ daughter threw her arms around him to comfort him, and she, too, turned to gold. “The golden touch is no blessing,” Midas cried.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is what Dionysus granted to King Midas. The very next sentence begins, "For his wish, Midas asked that whatever he touched would turn to gold." That reference back ("his wish") makes "wish" the only possible filler.

◦ Correct: Once there was a king named Midas who was granted a wish by Dionysus, the god of wine.

• The collocation "granted a wish" is a fixed expression in folk tales and mythology.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "slavery" (the state of being owned by another) is negative and completely out of context for a divine boon.

• Options 3 "employment" and 4 "job" refer to paid work; a god does not grant a king a "job", and neither word is echoed anywhere in the passage.

NOTE

• Contextual clue technique: in cloze passages, look for the word or idea repeated immediately after the blank. Here "For his wish" is a direct give-away.

• Collocations with "grant": grant a wish, grant permission, grant a request, grant a loan, take something for granted.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Once there was a king named Midas who was granted a (1)________ by Dionysus, the god of wine. For his wish, Midas asked that whatever he (2)________ would turn to gold. Despite Dionysus’ efforts to prevent it, Midas pleaded that this was a fantastic wish, and so, it was bestowed. Excited about his newly-earned (3)________, Midas started touching all kinds of things, turning each item into pure gold. But soon, Midas became (4)________. As he picked up a piece of food, he found he couldn’t eat it. It had turned to gold in his hand. Hungry, Midas groaned, “I’ll starve! Perhaps this was not such an excellent wish after all!” Seeing his dismay, Midas’ (5)________ daughter threw her arms around him to comfort him, and she, too, turned to gold. “The golden touch is no blessing,” Midas cried.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. touched.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The whole legend is about the "golden touch" of King Midas — whatever he touched turned to gold. The passage itself confirms this twice: "Midas started touching all kinds of things, turning each item into pure gold" and the closing line, "The golden touch is no blessing."

◦ Correct: For his wish, Midas asked that whatever he touched would turn to gold.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "next felt" is grammatically clumsy and makes no sense in the clause "whatever he next felt would turn to gold".

• Option 3 "kept" (retained) and Option 4 "left" (abandoned/departed from) contradict the later sentences, where the gold appears the moment he picks an object up, not when he keeps or leaves it.

NOTE

• General knowledge link: the expression "the Midas touch" is used today for a person who succeeds at, and profits from, everything he undertakes.

• Tense clue: the reporting structure "asked that whatever he ______ would turn" requires a simple past verb, which "touched", "kept" and "left" all satisfy — so the decision must be made on meaning, and only "touched" matches the story.

question: What is the maximum time gap between two sessions of the State Legislature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Six months.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 174(1) of the Constitution of India provides that the Governor shall summon the House (or each House) of the State Legislature at such time and place as he thinks fit, but six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.

• Thus the maximum gap between two sessions is six months, which effectively means the State Legislature must meet at least twice a year.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The same six-month rule applies to Parliament under Article 85(1).

• Powers of the Governor regarding the State Legislature:

◦ Summon and prorogue the House — Article 174(1) and 174(2)(a)

◦ Dissolve the Legislative Assembly — Article 174(2)(b)

◦ Address the House — Article 175; special address at the first session after each general election and at the first session of each year — Article 176

• A State Legislature consists of the Governor and one House (Vidhan Sabha) or two Houses (Vidhan Sabha + Vidhan Parishad) — Article 168.

NOTE

• The three usual sessions in a year are the Budget session, the Monsoon session and the Winter session.

• Article 172: normal term of a Legislative Assembly is five years, extendable by one year at a time during a National Emergency (and not beyond six months after the Emergency ends).

• The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is a permanent body that is never dissolved; one-third of its members retire every second year (Article 172(2)). Its creation or abolition is done by Parliament under Article 169 on a resolution of the State Assembly.

question: In 1951, the first Asian Games was held in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, from 4 to 11 March 1951.

• They were staged at the National Stadium (Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium), then called the Irwin Amphitheatre, and were inaugurated by the first President of India, Dr Rajendra Prasad.

• 11 countries took part with about 489 athletes competing in 6 sports (athletics, aquatics, basketball, cycling, football and weightlifting).

• Japan topped the medal tally; India finished second.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Asian Games are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA), founded in 1982; before that the body was the Asian Games Federation (AGF), founded in 1949 largely at the initiative of Prof. Guru Dutt Sondhi of India.

• Motto of the Asian Games: "Ever Onward".

• India has hosted the Asian Games twice — New Delhi 1951 and New Delhi 1982 (the 1982 mascot was Appu, the elephant).

NOTE

• Recent editions: 2014 – Incheon (South Korea), 2018 – Jakarta–Palembang (Indonesia), 2022 (held in 2023) – Hangzhou (China) where India won a record 107 medals (28 gold, 38 silver, 41 bronze).

• The next edition is scheduled for Aichi–Nagoya, Japan, in 2026.

question: What is a government budget?
option_1: A report on the economic growth of a country.
option_2: A plan for managing personal finances.
option_3: A financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period.
option_4: A document outlining foreign policy goals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A government budget is an annual financial statement showing the estimated receipts (revenue) and estimated expenditure of the government for a financial year, usually 1 April to 31 March in India.

• It is presented in Parliament under Article 112 of the Constitution, where it is called the "Annual Financial Statement".

• The budget has two broad parts:

◦ Revenue Budget – revenue receipts (tax and non-tax revenue) and revenue expenditure

◦ Capital Budget – capital receipts (borrowings, disinvestment, recovery of loans) and capital expenditure (asset creation)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 describe an economic survey/growth report, personal financial planning and a foreign-policy document respectively — none of these is a government budget.

• Types of budget:

◦ Balanced budget – estimated receipts = estimated expenditure

◦ Surplus budget – receipts > expenditure

◦ Deficit budget – expenditure > receipts (commonly used by developing economies)

• Important deficits: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings; Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts; Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments.

NOTE

• The first budget of independent India was presented by R. K. Shanmukham Chetty on 26 November 1947.

• The Union Budget is now presented on 1 February (shifted from the last working day of February in 2017), and the separate Railway Budget was merged with the Union Budget in 2017.

• The word "budget" comes from the French "bougette", meaning a small leather bag.

question: Which of the following oceans extends into the Mediterranean Sea?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Atlantic Ocean.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mediterranean Sea is connected to the Atlantic Ocean through the narrow Strait of Gibraltar, which lies between Spain (Europe) and Morocco (Africa) and is only about 14 km wide at its narrowest point.

• It is therefore an arm/marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean, almost completely enclosed by land — Europe to the north, Africa to the south and Asia to the east.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Mediterranean is also linked to the Red Sea through the man-made Suez Canal (opened in 1869), and to the Black Sea through the Dardanelles – Sea of Marmara – Bosphorus strait system.

• Its area is about 25 lakh sq km and its deepest point is the Calypso Deep in the Ionian Sea (about 5,267 m).

• The name "Mediterranean" comes from the Latin "medius" (middle) + "terra" (land) — the sea in the middle of the land.

NOTE

• The five oceans by size: Pacific > Atlantic > Indian > Southern (Antarctic) > Arctic.

• The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest ocean and has the shape of the letter "S"; the Mid-Atlantic Ridge runs through it.

• Important straits to remember: Strait of Gibraltar (Atlantic–Mediterranean), Strait of Hormuz (Persian Gulf–Gulf of Oman), Strait of Malacca (Indian Ocean–Pacific), Palk Strait (India–Sri Lanka), Bering Strait (Asia–North America).

question: What is the meaning of the term ‘Collateral’ in banking?
option_4: An asset pledged as security for a loan
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An asset pledged as security for a loan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In banking, "collateral" means an asset (such as land, a building, gold, shares, fixed deposits or machinery) that a borrower pledges to a lender as security against a loan.

• If the borrower defaults, the lender has the legal right to seize and sell the collateral to recover the money lent. Collateral therefore reduces the lender's credit risk.

• Loans backed by collateral are called "secured loans" (e.g., home loans, gold loans, car loans); loans without it are "unsecured loans" (e.g., personal loans, credit-card dues), which carry higher interest rates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 describe an investment portfolio, a credit instrument and a payment mode respectively — none is collateral.

• Related banking terms:

◦ Mortgage – security created on immovable property

◦ Pledge – security created on movable goods where possession passes to the lender

◦ Hypothecation – security on movable goods where possession stays with the borrower

◦ NPA (Non-Performing Asset) – a loan on which interest/principal is overdue for more than 90 days

• Under the SARFAESI Act, 2002, banks can take possession of secured assets of defaulters without going to court.

NOTE

• Under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana, Stand-Up India and the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), small loans are given without collateral.

• The RBI has also raised the collateral-free agricultural loan limit in recent years to help small and marginal farmers.

question: The word ‘kathak’ is derived from which of the following words?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Story.

• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha", which means "story", and "Kathakar" means "one who tells a story".

• Kathak began with the Kathakars — wandering bards and storytellers of northern India who narrated episodes from the epics and Puranas through gesture, music and dance in temples and village squares.

• It is the classical dance of North India, especially Uttar Pradesh, and is famous for rapid footwork (tatkar), chakkars (spins) and expressive abhinaya.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathak flourished in both temple (bhakti) and Mughal court traditions, which gave rise to its main gharanas:

◦ Lucknow gharana – emphasis on expression/abhinaya (Bindadin Maharaj, Birju Maharaj)

◦ Jaipur gharana – emphasis on footwork and rhythm/layakari

◦ Banaras gharana – Janakiprasad

◦ Raigarh gharana – patronised by Raja Chakradhar Singh

• Famous exponents: Pandit Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj, Gopi Krishna, Kumudini Lakhia, Shovana Narayan, Pandit Durgalal.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi:

◦ Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu

◦ Kathak – Uttar Pradesh

◦ Kathakali and Mohiniyattam – Kerala

◦ Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh

◦ Odissi – Odisha

◦ Manipuri – Manipur

◦ Sattriya – Assam

• Kathak is accompanied by the tabla and pakhawaj, and the dancer wears ghungroos (ankle bells).

question: In relation to the state of Tamil Nadu, the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2022 will include the __________ and Kurivikkaran communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes in Tamil Nadu.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Narikoravan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2022 added the Narikoravan and Kurivikkaran communities to the list of Scheduled Tribes of Tamil Nadu.

• These are traditionally nomadic, hunting-and-gathering communities; they were earlier classified as a Most Backward Class / Denotified Community, and the amendment gave them ST status with the accompanying benefits of reservation in education, employment and government welfare schemes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2, 3 and 4 — Irular, Kadar and Kammara — were already notified as Scheduled Tribes in Tamil Nadu, so they could not be "included" by this Act.

• Under Article 342 of the Constitution, the President, after consulting the Governor of the State, specifies the tribes to be treated as Scheduled Tribes; only Parliament can then add to or remove names from that list by law.

• Tamil Nadu has 36 notified Scheduled Tribes; prominent ones are the Toda, Kota, Badaga (an OBC in some lists), Kurumba, Irula, Paniyan and Kattunayakan of the Nilgiris.

• Related constitutional provisions: Article 341 (Scheduled Castes), Article 342 (Scheduled Tribes), Article 342A (Socially and Educationally Backward Classes, inserted by the 102nd Amendment).

question: Which antibiotic is considered the first miracle drug, used to treat throat infections, meningitis, syphilis and other bacterial infections?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Penicillin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Penicillin was the world's first true antibiotic and is universally called the "miracle drug" because it dramatically cut deaths from bacterial infections such as streptococcal throat infection, pneumonia, meningitis, syphilis, gonorrhoea, diphtheria and rheumatic fever.

• It was discovered accidentally in 1928 by Sir Alexander Fleming at St Mary's Hospital, London, from the mould Penicillium notatum (now P. rubens), which had contaminated a culture plate of Staphylococcus.

• Howard Florey and Ernst Boris Chain later purified it and made mass production possible during the Second World War. Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1945.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Penicillin works by inhibiting the synthesis of the bacterial cell wall (it blocks peptidoglycan cross-linking), so it is bactericidal and mainly effective against Gram-positive bacteria.

• Option 1 Aciclovir is an antiviral drug (used for herpes and chickenpox), not an antibiotic.

• Option 2 Nifuratel is an antimicrobial used mainly for genito-urinary infections.

• Option 4 Metronidazole is used against anaerobic bacteria and protozoa (amoebiasis, giardiasis, trichomoniasis).

NOTE

• Other landmark antibiotics: Streptomycin (Selman Waksman, 1943 — first effective drug against tuberculosis), Sulfa drugs/Prontosil (Gerhard Domagk), Tetracycline, Chloramphenicol, Erythromycin.

• Antibiotics are ineffective against viruses; their misuse causes antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a major global health concern.

question: Which of the following is the Fundamental Law of any country which sets out the framework and the principal functions of various organs of the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Constitution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Constitution is the fundamental (supreme) law of a country. It lays down the framework of government, defines the structure, powers and functions of the legislature, executive and judiciary, distributes power between the Centre and the States, and guarantees the rights and duties of citizens.

• Every other law must conform to it; a law that violates the Constitution can be declared void by the courts (the doctrine of judicial review, Articles 13, 32 and 226).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Customs" are long-established usages and traditions; they may be a source of law but are not the fundamental law.

• Option 2 "International Law" governs relations between States, not the internal organs of one government.

• Option 4 "Ordinance" is a temporary law promulgated by the President (Article 123) or a Governor (Article 213) when the legislature is not in session; it must be laid before the legislature and ceases to operate six weeks after it reassembles.

NOTE

• The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. It is the longest written constitution in the world.

• The Constituent Assembly was formed in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan; Dr Rajendra Prasad was its President and Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

• Originally it had 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; at present it has about 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

• The Basic Structure doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati case, 1973) holds that Parliament cannot amend the essential features of the Constitution.

question: Rani Machaiah was awarded with ‘Padam Shri’ in the year ________ for her contribution to folk dance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 2023.

• Rani Machaiah of Kodagu (Coorg), Karnataka, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2023 in the field of Art (folk dance).

• She is renowned for popularising and preserving "Ummathat", the traditional folk dance of Kodava women, performed in colourful Kodava attire during the Kailpodhu and Puthari festivals; she has trained thousands of women in the form over several decades.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Padma Awards, instituted in 1954, are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day and conferred by the President of India at Rashtrapati Bhavan, usually in March/April.

• They are given in three grades:

◦ Padma Vibhushan – exceptional and distinguished service (highest)

◦ Padma Bhushan – distinguished service of a high order

◦ Padma Shri – distinguished service

• The awards cover fields such as art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, civil service and sports.

• Padma awards are not conferred posthumously as a rule (exceptions are made in highly deserving cases) and carry no cash allowance.

NOTE

question: Which physicist's experiment during a lecture in 1820 showed the connection between electricity and magnetism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Hans Christian Oersted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1820, while demonstrating an experiment during a lecture, the Danish physicist Hans Christian Oersted noticed that a magnetic compass needle placed near a current-carrying wire was deflected.

• This accidental observation proved for the first time that an electric current produces a magnetic field, establishing the link between electricity and magnetism and giving birth to the science of electromagnetism.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 John Cockcroft (with Ernest Walton) first split the atom using a particle accelerator (Nobel Prize, 1951).

• Option 2 William Gilbert wrote "De Magnete" (1600) and showed that the Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet; he is called the father of the study of magnetism and electricity.

• Option 3 Heinrich Hertz experimentally produced and detected electromagnetic waves (1887), confirming Maxwell's theory; the SI unit of frequency, the hertz (Hz), is named after him.

NOTE

• The CGS unit of magnetic field strength, the "oersted" (Oe), is named after Hans Christian Oersted.

• Related laws:

◦ Right-hand thumb rule / Maxwell's corkscrew rule – direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor

◦ Ampere's circuital law – relates magnetic field to current

◦ Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction (1831) – a changing magnetic field produces an electric current (the converse of Oersted's finding)

◦ Fleming's left-hand rule (motors) and right-hand rule (generators)

question: In the performance of ________ dance, on one side raasa dances are performed by women, whereas on the opposite side instrumentalist play the pung choloms (drums) and the karataala (cymbals).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Manipuri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Manipuri is the classical dance of the state of Manipur. Its central theme is the Raas Leela — the love story of Radha and Krishna — performed with gentle, flowing, rounded movements.

• A Manipuri performance has two clear halves: the Raas (Jagoi) danced by women, and, on the other side, the Sankirtana performed by male instrumentalists playing the Pung (Pung Cholom, the barrel drum) and the Kartal/Karataala (cymbals, Kartal Cholom).

• Costume: the women wear the stiff, cylindrical, richly embroidered skirt called the "Potloi/Kumin" with a translucent veil.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Kathakali – Kerala; elaborate make-up (chutti), huge headgear, all-male dance-drama based on epics.

• Option 2 Yakshagana – a folk/traditional theatre form of coastal Karnataka, not one of the eight classical dances.

• Option 3 Odissi – Odisha; characterised by the tribhanga posture and chowk stance, and by sculpture-like poses inspired by temple carvings.

• Famous Manipuri exponents: the Jhaveri sisters (Nayana, Suverna, Ranjana, Darshana), Guru Bipin Singh, Sonarik Singh, Charu Mathur.

NOTE

• Rabindranath Tagore introduced Manipuri dance at Santiniketan in 1919, which gave it national recognition.

• Lai Haraoba is the ritual festival of Manipur from which many of the dance's movements derive; Thang-Ta is the martial art of Manipur.

• The UNESCO recognised Sankirtana, ritual singing, drumming and dancing of Manipur as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2013.

question: Who among the following was the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgars, a powerful non-violent movement among the Pathans of North-West Frontier Province?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1890–1988) founded the Khudai Khidmatgar ("Servants of God") movement in 1929 among the Pathans (Pashtuns) of the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP).

• Because of their red-coloured uniforms the members were popularly known as the "Surkh Posh" or "Red Shirts". The movement was strictly non-violent and worked for social reform, education and the freedom struggle in close alliance with the Indian National Congress.

• Ghaffar Khan was affectionately called "Frontier Gandhi", "Badshah Khan" and "Bacha Khan".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987 — the first non-Indian citizen to receive it.

• He opposed the Partition of India and famously told the Congress leaders, "You have thrown us to the wolves."

• Option 4 Khan Abdul Jabbar Khan (Dr Khan Sahib) was his elder brother and the Congress Premier of NWFP.

• Option 3 Mohammad Ali Jinnah founded Pakistan and led the Muslim League, which opposed the Khudai Khidmatgars in the frontier.

NOTE

• The Qissa Khwani Bazaar massacre at Peshawar (23 April 1930) during the Civil Disobedience Movement saw Khudai Khidmatgars shot at by British troops; the Garhwal Rifles soldiers famously refused to fire on the unarmed crowd.

• Ghaffar Khan's newspaper/journal was "Pakhtoon"; his autobiography is "My Life and Struggle".

question: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 1878 CE.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 by Lord Lytton, the Viceroy of India (1876–1880), to curb criticism of British rule in Indian-language (vernacular) newspapers.

• It empowered magistrates to demand a bond and security deposit from the printer/publisher of a vernacular paper, to forfeit the press and machinery if the undertaking was violated, and gave no right of appeal in a court of law.

• Because it applied only to Indian-language papers and not to English-language ones, it was called the "Gagging Act".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The immediate victim was "Amrita Bazar Patrika", which overnight converted itself into an English newspaper to escape the Act.

• The Act was repealed in 1882 by Lord Ripon, who is also known for the Local Self-Government Resolution (1882) and the first Factory Act (1881); he is called the "Father of Local Self-Government in India".

• Other repressive measures of Lord Lytton: the Arms Act, 1878, the grand Delhi Durbar of 1877 during a severe famine, and the lowering of the maximum age for the Indian Civil Service examination from 21 to 19.

NOTE

• Landmark press regulations in British India:

◦ 1799 – Censorship of Press Act (Lord Wellesley)

◦ 1823 – Licensing Regulations (John Adams); "Mirat-ul-Akhbar" of Raja Ram Mohan Roy closed down

◦ 1835 – Metcalfe Act, the "Liberator of the Indian Press"

◦ 1857 – Licensing Act

◦ 1878 – Vernacular Press Act (Lytton)

◦ 1908 – Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act

◦ 1910 – Indian Press Act

question: Which state of India is associated with the famous thunderstorms ‘Kaal Baisakhi’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. West Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kaal Baisakhi" (also called Nor'westers) are violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms that strike West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Assam during March–May, most typically in the Bengali month of Baisakh — hence the name, meaning "the calamity of Baisakh".

• They come as sudden squalls with strong winds, lightning, torrential rain and sometimes hail, usually in the late afternoon or evening, and can cause considerable damage to life and property.

• In Assam the same storms are called "Bardoli Chheerha"; they benefit tea, jute and rice crops.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other important local winds and pre-monsoon showers of India:

◦ Loo – hot, dry, scorching wind of the northern plains in May–June

◦ Mango Showers – pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and Karnataka that help mangoes ripen

◦ Blossom Shower – pre-monsoon rain in Kerala/Karnataka that helps coffee flowers bloom

◦ Cherry Blossom / Coffee Blossom – Karnataka

◦ Aandhi – dust storms of north India

NOTE

• Kaal Baisakhi storms occur when hot, dry air from the Chhotanagpur plateau meets warm, moist air from the Bay of Bengal, producing towering cumulonimbus clouds.

• The October–November period brings the retreating (north-east) monsoon and cyclones to the Coromandel coast, while the pre-monsoon season is dominated by thunderstorms of this type.

question: According to Ministry of Commerce and Industry (2018-19), which state of India is the largest producer of Rubber?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kerala is by far the largest producer of natural rubber in India, accounting for roughly 70–75 per cent of the country's total production, followed by Tripura and Tamil Nadu.

• Rubber is an equatorial/tropical plantation crop that requires:

◦ a hot and humid climate with temperature above 25 °C

◦ rainfall above 200 cm, well distributed through the year

◦ deep, well-drained laterite soil

Kerala's climate along the Western Ghats meets all these conditions perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Rubber Board of India (established under the Rubber Act, 1947) has its headquarters at Kottayam, Kerala.

• India is among the top rubber-producing countries in the world; Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam lead globally.

• Rubber was brought to India by the British; the first commercial plantations came up in Kerala in the late nineteenth century. Rubber is obtained by tapping latex from the tree Hevea brasiliensis, originally from the Amazon basin.

NOTE

• Other leading states for plantation crops:

◦ Tea – Assam (largest), then West Bengal

◦ Coffee – Karnataka (largest), then Kerala and Tamil Nadu

◦ Coconut – Kerala/Tamil Nadu

◦ Spices (black pepper, cardamom) – Kerala

◦ Cashew – Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha

• Tripura is called the "second rubber capital of India."

question: ‘Losoong’ festival, celebrated by the tribal community in ___________, is usually the time when the farmers rejoice and celebrate their harvest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sikkim.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Losoong" (also spelt Namsoong among the Lepchas) is the Sikkimese New Year and harvest festival, celebrated mainly by the Bhutia and Lepcha communities of Sikkim, usually in December, at the end of the harvest season.

• Farmers rejoice over the year's produce; the festival is marked by Chaam (masked lama dances) in monasteries such as Rumtek, Phodong and Tsuklakhang, archery competitions, feasting and the local drink chhang.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

• Other festivals of Sikkim: Saga Dawa, Pang Lhabsol (worship of Mount Khangchendzonga), Bhumchu, Drukpa Tshechi, Tendong Lho Rum Faat.

◦ Pongal – Tamil Nadu

◦ Makar Sankranti – across India; Magh Bihu – Assam

◦ Baisakhi – Punjab; Lohri – Punjab/Haryana

◦ Onam – Kerala; Nuakhai – Odisha

◦ Sarhul and Karma – Jharkhand

◦ Ka Sohrai / Bandna – Jharkhand and West Bengal

NOTE

• Sikkim became the 22nd state of India in 1975 (36th Constitutional Amendment). Its capital is Gangtok, and Khangchendzonga, the world's third highest peak, lies on its border.

question: According to the Human Development Index 2021, which group of neighbouring countries has ranked behind India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pakistan and Afghanistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Human Development Report 2021-22 released by the UNDP, India was ranked 132nd out of 191 countries with an HDI value of 0.633 (Medium Human Development category).

• Among India's neighbours, Pakistan (161) and Afghanistan (180) ranked behind (lower than) India, while Sri Lanka (73), China (79), Maldives (90), Bhutan (127) and Bangladesh (129) all ranked ahead of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Human Development Index (HDI) was created by the Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq with Amartya Sen and was first published in the Human Development Report of 1990.

• The HDI is a composite index of three dimensions:

◦ Health – life expectancy at birth

◦ Education – mean years of schooling (adults 25+) and expected years of schooling (children)

◦ Standard of living – Gross National Income (GNI) per capita at PPP

• Its value ranges from 0 to 1, and countries are grouped as Very High (0.800+), High, Medium and Low human development.

• Switzerland topped the 2021 index, followed by Norway and Iceland; South Sudan was last.

NOTE

• Other UNDP indices: Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI), Gender Inequality Index (GII), Gender Development Index (GDI) and the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI).

• India's HDI has risen steadily since 1990; the 2021 dip in global HDI values was largely attributed to the COVID-19 pandemic, which lowered life expectancy worldwide.

question: Which of the following statements is true about the Great Bath of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
option_1: It was used for grain storage.
option_3: It was used as the water tank of the city.
option_4: It was probably used for religious purpose.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. It was probably used for religious purpose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Great Bath was found at Mohenjo-daro (on the bank of the Indus in Sindh, present-day Pakistan), discovered by R. D. Banerji in 1922.

• It is a large rectangular tank inside the citadel, measuring about 11.88 m × 7.01 m and 2.43 m deep, with flights of steps at the north and south ends, a surrounding corridor and small rooms on one side.

• Scholars believe it was used for ritual bathing / religious ceremonial purposes, not for ordinary domestic water supply — hence it is regarded as evidence of the ritual importance of water in Harappan life.

• Its waterproofing is remarkable: bricks laid on edge with gypsum mortar and a layer of natural bitumen (tar) to prevent seepage; water was drawn from a well and drained out through a corbelled drain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because grain was stored in the Great Granary, a separate structure at Mohenjo-daro (and at Harappa).

• Options 2 and 3 do not fit its location inside the citadel, its steps or its elaborate ritual design.

• Other important Mohenjo-daro finds: the Great Granary, the Assembly Hall, the bronze Dancing Girl, the steatite Bearded Priest-King, and the Pashupati seal.

NOTE

• Key Harappan sites and their finds:

◦ Harappa (Ravi, Pakistan; Daya Ram Sahni, 1921) – granaries, cemetery R-37

◦ Lothal (Gujarat) – dockyard, rice husk, fire altars

◦ Dholavira (Gujarat) – water reservoirs, signboard; UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021)

◦ Kalibangan (Rajasthan) – ploughed field, fire altars

◦ Rakhigarhi (Haryana) – the largest Harappan site in India

◦ Chanhudaro (Sindh) – bead-making, the only site without a citadel
